Annotators mark each Semantic Content Unit (SCU) as "present" if it can be inferred from the system summary, otherwise "not present"; majority vote determines final SCU presence.

Workers are presented with a system summary and a set of Semantic Content Units (SCUs) extracted from the reference summary, and asked to mark each SCU as 'present' if it can be inferred from the system summary or 'not present' otherwise.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated multiple guideline descriptions into one comprehensive statement, normalized 'SCU presence' criterion to the broader 'content selection' category it belongs to

overall_notes: The extraction was generally good but contained some duplicate items and formatting inconsistencies. The paper focuses on meta-evaluation of summarization metrics using both automatic metrics and human evaluations based on the Pyramid method. No LLM evaluation was used. The human evaluation specifically assesses content selection using Semantic Content Units (SCUs) extracted from reference summaries.
